content: {"summary":"On 21 April 2025 a new prod.internal zone file was pushed to internal‑dns‑02 and CoreDNS was restarted. The zone lacked the auth‑database DNS record, which was still present on the other internal DNS server. auth‑service‑01’s DNS queries were forwarded to both servers; each query randomly hit either server and cached the result for up to 30 seconds, so the service saw alternating NXDOMAIN failures and successes.","likely_cause":"Missing auth‑database DNS record in the zone file deployed to internal‑dns‑02, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN responses due to round‑robin DNS forwarding and short‑lived caching.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"internal‑dns‑02 received a new prod.internal zone file and restarted CoreDNS","evidence_ids":["INC-0033#0"],"quote":"New `prod.internal` zone file placed and `coredns` restarted."},{"text":"The auth database DNS record was missing on internal‑dns‑02 but present on the other DNS server","evidence_ids":["INC-0033#1"],"quote":"The auth database record was found missing on internal-dns-02 and present on the other server."},{"text":"auth‑service‑01 saw alternating NXDOMAIN failures because CoreDNS randomly queried the two DNS servers and cached each response for up to 30 seconds","evidence_ids":["INC-0033#0"],"quote":"Every cache refill was thus a coin toss between the intact server and internal-dns-02"}],"next_checks":["Verify the contents of the prod.internal zone file on internal-dns-02 for the missing record","Confirm that both internal DNS servers now contain identical zone data","Check CoreDNS forwarding and cache settings to ensure consistent resolution","Review the zone‑push process to add validation for required records"]}
